name: Hydrolyzed hyaluronic acid
lead: Hydrolyzed hyaluronic acid is hyaluronic acid (HA) that has been broken into shorter chains, and it is marketed in skincare as a low-molecular-weight form intended for deeper hydration. HA itself is a glycosaminoglycan found in skin and other connective tissues, where it supports hydration [1].

Encyclopedia coverage of HA notes that chain length matters biologically: high-molecular-weight HA and low-molecular-weight fragments behave differently in cell studies, and some very small fragments have been reported to promote angiogenesis and inflammatory responses [1][2]. That coverage does not address how well topically applied hydrolyzed HA penetrates skin [1].
Published clinical evidence specific to hydrolyzed HA as a topical ingredient is limited to a small number of studies of multi-ingredient products.

paras: Hyaluronic acid chains in the body range from a few thousand daltons to millions. Acid or alkaline hydrolysis, ultrasound, heat and oxidants can degrade HA into smaller pieces [1]. Cosmetic products list the shortened forms as hydrolyzed hyaluronic acid.

Karl Meyer and John Palmer first isolated hyaluronic acid in 1934 from bovine vitreous [1]. A 1953 paper in Science examined a diffusible component of hydrolyzed HA in relation to vaccinia virus inactivation [3]. A 1985 Science paper reported that HA degradation products induced angiogenesis [2].

In cell studies summarised in encyclopedia coverage, HA above about 500 kDa stimulated HA synthesis in cultured synovial fibroblasts, while low-molecular-weight HA at high concentrations inhibited it [1]. Degradation fragments have been reported to trigger inflammatory responses in immune cells [1].
Hydrolyzed HA is promoted in serums as a smaller molecule meant to reach deeper than standard HA. The wiki's sources contain no looksmaxxing-forum discussion specific to it.

No controlled trials of hydrolyzed hyaluronic acid alone as a topical were found. One preprint reported a face serum combining bakuchiol, palmitoyl tripeptide-38, hydrolyzed HA and a polyherbal and vitamin blend; it was tested in vitro, in a patch test in 55 healthy adults (no irritation or allergic contact dermatitis reported) and in a human efficacy trial, with the authors reporting improved skin quality [4]. Because the product had many ingredients, the contribution of hydrolyzed HA cannot be separated. Lab work has also used hydrolyzed HA gels to make microneedles [5].

card.summary: Chopped-up hyaluronic acid sold as the deeper-penetrating hydrator; direct evidence is thin.
card.note: No standalone topical trials; very small HA fragments have shown pro-inflammatory activity in cell studies.

quick.overview:
Hydrolyzed hyaluronic acid is hyaluronic acid broken into shorter chains. Brands market it as getting deeper into skin than regular HA.

The only human data found come from a multi-ingredient serum, so its own effect has not been isolated.
quick.mechanism: HA binds water and supports skin hydration; shorter chains are argued to reach further, though encyclopedia coverage does not address topical penetration.
quick.risks: A patch test of a serum containing it reported no irritation or allergy in 55 adults. Laboratory work shows small HA fragments can provoke inflammatory responses in cells.
